newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bank base rate fall a "psychological" lift.
newsitem.headline: French bank base rate fall a "psychological" lift.

text.p: The decision by French commercial banks to cut base lending rates offers a psychological boost which can only help the economy, even if the direct impact is very marginal, economists said on Friday.
"It's more symbolic than effective on the economy," said ABN Amro economist Philippe Brossard.
Base lending rates applied to a relatively limited amount of funding, he noted. "(But) Certainly it's a positive factor."
Leading French banks said on Friday they were cutting base rates, effective Monday, to 6.55 from 6.75 percent, following drops in official and market interest rates.
Analyst David Naude at JP Morgan in Paris said the base rate reduction was a logical adjustment to the steady lowering of official and money market interest rates.
"Basically, commercial banks are doing their bit by adjusting slowly to the easing in money rates," Naude said.
"At the margin, this is good news because it tells us the economy will eventually benefit from monetary easing," he said.
On Thursday, the Bank of France made the latest in a series of small cuts in official interest rates, with a cut of 10 basis points in the key intervention rate to 3.25 from 3.35 percent.

Brossard at ABN Amro in Paris said the next step to look for would be a government decision to cut the interest rate offered on housing savings plans and to make another cut in the rate offered on the popular Livret A savings account product backed by the state.
